chapter: Shelly Manne, the Candolis and 1957 records
title: Richie Kamuca
summary: Met in Kenton's band, a Lester Young-influenced player who excelled at the Blackhawk and later died of cancer.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Some of the other members of the orchestra on this date, The Fabulous Bill Holman, include one of your reedmates, who seems to recur on several of your projects, Richie Kamuca. Did I pronounce that correctly?
Could you talk a little bit about Richie?

I met Richie when he joined Kenton‟s band in ‟52. He was from Philadelphia, good friends, family. They worked a lot together. A Lester Young. He had a lazy, floating way of playing, not unlike Pres. I‟m trying to think. I guess he left Kenton‟s band when Zoot joined. I don‟t know if he moved to L.A. at that time or went back to Philly, but he eventually wound up out here and eventually played with Shelly‟s quintet after Charlie Mariano left. A wonderful player. Shelly made a few CDs from their gig up in San Francisco at – I forget what club it was. It was a well known jazz club.

Yeah, the Blackhawk. That was the best I ever heard Richie play. He really sounded like somebody lit a fire under him. He had a basic Lester thing, but all of a sudden all this energy. I‟m sure glad he got to make that record, because it really adds to his catalogue. He was part Italian, part Filipino. That‟s where his name came from.
Did he die early as well?
Yeah. He got cancer. He was doing The Merv Griffin Show after they moved out here and got cancer and went fairly quickly.
